scope: Bounded consumer inspection for effective-only CES endpoint and missing entitlement IDs.

claims.statement: Shared permission helper derives entitlements from entity.name, subject.name and action.name or checks flat user.entitlement.actions. Its X_RATANONE branch checks feature/action names. Numeric entitlement identifiers are not used in these checks.
claims.limit: Bounded helper paths only; not every application consumer.

claims.statement: Profile UI uses subject.id and entity.id in accordion DOM IDs, and entity.id as a React key. Dropping all IDs without changing this consumer leaves missing-key/identifier compatibility risks.
claims.limit: No browser execution; tangible deployed impact not established.

claims.statement: Action, Subject and Entity TypeScript interfaces require numeric id fields; Action also requires entitlementId and Entity roleId.
claims.limit: Type declarations do not themselves prove a runtime decision uses those fields.

claims.statement: Frontend admin role helper selects exact entity name FMO PORTAL ADMIN and returns roleName.
claims.limit: roleName is a compatibility requirement separate from numeric IDs.

claims.statement: Entitlement-token projection keys subjects/actions under entityName:roleName. It reads action names and does not require action IDs.
claims.limit: Does not establish how a missing roleName should be mapped from multiple CES role names.

claims.statement: Admin token validation extracts the role name from an entitlement key prefixed by configured admin entity. It supplies ems2Role for authorization.
claims.limit: Configured owner scope and approved CES admin role mappings remain unknown.

claims.statement: CES result mapper populates entity names and subject/action names but does not populate entity.id, roleId, roleName, subject.id, action.id or action.entitlementId.
claims.limit: This is current source; not proof all consumers tolerate missing fields.

claims.statement: CES-controlled drawer visibility uses configured entity names, EMS3 source tags and per-tile granted IDs. The numeric tile IDs identify application configuration, not EMS2/CES entitlement IDs.
claims.limit: Do not remove required tile IDs when changing entitlement identity fields.

claims.statement: Entitlement entity merge keys contain name, roleId and roleName. Numeric role ID remains part of this legacy-compatible grouping shape.
claims.limit: A nullable grouping component does not itself prove a failure; no execution performed.

claims.statement: The EMS2 adapter uses numeric roleId to associate grants and subject.id to group actions. This is the legacy retrieval transformation; the CES mapper has a separate name-based transformation.
claims.limit: Missing CES IDs should not be passed through this EMS2 reconstruction path unchanged.

claims.statement: Tile administration forwards extracted ems2Role into role checks and role-scoped data selection.
claims.limit: No approved replacement admin ownership contract or runtime verification in this stage.

conclusion: Name-based feature/action authorization can use effective grants without provider numeric IDs. Existing profile UI, declared types, grouping and roleName-dependent administration require explicit compatibility treatment. No universal safe-removal claim is supported.
limits: Static source and bounded searches only; no browser, unit or integration test executed.
mfe-ratan-container is a supplied filesystem source; no independent Git history is established.
Existing unrelated local changes were not modified.
Any local display key or compatibility alias must remain distinct from an authoritative CES identifier or authorization grant.
